issues.description: Module-import side effect mutates a private SDK global READ_BUFFER_SIZE
issues.detail: `genai._api_client.READ_BUFFER_SIZE = 5 * 1024 * 1024` runs at import time, touches a private attribute, and silently changes behavior for every consumer of google-genai in the process. This complects a per-call need (large image payloads) with global place-oriented state and a private API contract. Pass the buffer size as data through the call, or open an upstream issue rather than mutating a private place.

issues.description: OutputImageRawFrame is constructed with raw RGB bytes but the image may not be RGB
issues.detail: `Image.open(...).tobytes()` returns bytes in whatever mode PIL inferred (often RGBA or P for PNG), yet the frame is hardcoded `format="RGB"`. Value and its declared type are complected: the label lies about the bytes. Convert explicitly (`image.convert("RGB")`) or pass the actual mode through, so the value and its description agree.

issues.description: Image-model detection by substring `"image" in model_name` complects naming with capability
issues.detail: `if "image" in self._model_name` treats the model string as both an identity and a capability declaration. Any future model whose name contains "image" silently inherits the no-thinking-budget rule. Make capability a value (a set of known image models, or a typed flag on the model record) rather than a substring guess on an identity.

issues.description: Default model bump is a silent behavior change shipped under "Added"
issues.detail: Changing the default from `gemini-2.0-flash` to `gemini-2.5-flash` changes the value every existing caller resolves to without opting in. It is noted under Changed in the changelog but is effectively a breaking default. Either keep the prior default and require opt-in, or call this out as a breaking change with a migration note; do not complect "add image support" with "swap everyone's model".

issues.description: Image part handling is inlined into a long candidate-processing loop instead of decomposed
issues.detail: The new `elif part.inline_data` branch sits inside an already deeply nested for/if chain that mixes text, function calls, and now image bytes. The essential operation is simple: map a Part to a Frame. Pull a small pure function `part_to_frame(part) -> Frame | None` so the loop just iterates and pushes; the complecting of dispatch with side-effecting `push_frame` is incidental.

issues.description: No tests or assertions accompany the new image path; the "temporary hack" has no expiry
issues.detail: A comment labeled "Temporary hack" with a magic 5 MiB constant has no test pinning the behavior and no issue link or TODO with conditions for removal. Temporary state without a recorded time semantics tends to become permanent. Record the upstream issue, the version where it can be removed, and add at least one test exercising an inline_data response.

review.summary: The feature is small and mostly clean, but it leans on three pieces of incidental complexity: a module-level mutation of a private SDK global, a substring sniff to classify the model, and a hardcoded `format=\"RGB\"` that may not match the PIL image's actual mode. The default-model swap is a silent value change for every existing caller and should be separated from the image-generation work. Decomposing the inline_data branch into a small pure `part -> frame` function would make the candidate loop simple rather than just shorter. The hammock question that should have been asked first: what is the actual value here — a stream of typed Parts from Gemini — and where should the place-oriented buffer size live, if anywhere in this process?
